title: Guard the External Call
description: A withdraw entrypoint updates a balance and then calls an external token contract. Soroban does not stop a malicious token contract from calling back into the game. Choose the ordering that prevents the callback from draining the balance twice.

content.prompt: Which sequence correctly combines checks-effects-interactions with a storage-backed reentrancy lock around the external token call?
options: Set the lock, call the token contract, check the lock, then clear it.
Check that the lock is clear, set the lock, apply the balance change, call the token contract, then clear the lock on both the success and error paths.
Call the token contract first, then check the lock and update the balance.
Rely on `require_auth` from the player; an authorized caller can never re-enter.

solution: Check that the lock is clear, set the lock, apply the balance change, call the token contract, then clear the lock on both the success and error paths.
hint: Reentrancy protection needs state that is written *before* the external call and read by the reentrant invocation. Apply the balance change before the call (checks-effects-interactions), persist the lock, and clear it after the call returns or fails so a single failure cannot brick the entrypoint. Authorization proves who called; it does not prove the call is not re-entering.
author: StellarHunts Core

testCases.title: Checking after the call is too late
Calling out before updating state enables double spend
